sections.text: Alaska Airlines identified guests were spending 40-plus hours in planning trips and rarely using AlaskaAir.com’s Where We Fly tool, making travel discovery overwhelming and impersonal.

sections.title: Looking ahead to AI as the heart of transformation
sections.text: With direct access to Microsoft experts, Alaska Airlines avoids common deployment challenges, fine-tuning model responses, eliminating hallucinations, and ensuring pricing and destination data remain accurate. And as Alaska Airlines completes its acquisition of Hawaiian Airlines, it’s ramping up business process transformation with AI at the center.

sections.title: Executive summary
sections.text: Copilot’s rapid growth introduced complex, long-running AI workflows at massive scale, but fragmented retry logic and custom recovery made it difficult to ensure reliability and maintain engineering velocity.

sections.title: READ THE STORY
sections.text: Microsoft Copilot serves hundreds of millions of people. On the surface, the experience feels simple. Answer a question, summarize content, draft an email, manage a schedule. But Copilot is no longer just a conversational interface. It is a platform with increasingly diverse capabilities, each operating at massive scale.

sections.title: Why retry loops were not enough
sections.text: As these background workloads grew, so did the engineering challenge. A traditional queue and retry approach can move work through a system, but it leaves teams responsible for correctness over time. If a workflow fails halfway through, after validating a task but before scheduling the next recurrence, or after fetching user preferences, but before ranking results, teams need custom logic to resume from that exact point. They need idempotency, state checkpoints, and decisions about what data persists, where the failure occurred, and how to resume without duplicating work.

sections.title: One reliability model, 25+ orchestrations
sections.text: The power of standardizing on DTS became clear not in any single orchestration, but in the breadth of workloads it could handle. Copilot now uses DTS across 25+ orchestrations in 10+ microservices, with workflows authored using the Durable Task SDKs in services running on Azure Kubernetes Service all following the same reliability pattern.

sections.title: Deliberate rollout, compounding results
sections.text: The rollout was deliberate. Copilot applied the same DTS powered resilience model across different workload shapes as new needs emerged, rather than adopting a separate reliability approach for each one. Each additional use case reinforced the same lesson. Once durability lived in the orchestration layer, teams could keep the programming model consistent while the platform handled persistence, recovery, and replay underneath.

sections.title: Impact at scale
sections.text: The real shift was operational. Durable orchestration became a repeatable standard across teams and services, allowing new capabilities to plug into an existing resilience model instead of rebuilding one.

sections.title: A blueprint for AI scale orchestration
sections.text: For engineering and platform leaders, the Copilot story reflects a clear systems design choice. Place durability in the orchestration layer rather than in individual features. Durable timers, replay based recovery, and sub orchestration composition reduce custom reliability work while supporting high throughput across heterogeneous AI workloads.

title: How Premera Blue Cross strengthened the heartbeat of its business with Microsoft Azure
description: Premera Blue Cross modernized its mission-critical FACETS platform on Microsoft Azure, improving performance and building a foundation for future innovation.

sections.title: Executive summary
sections.text: Premera needed to modernize TriZetto® Facets®, its mission-critical payer platform, without disrupting claims processing. The organization sought greater resilience, scalability, and a foundation for future innovation while protecting the experience of members and providers.

sections.title: The heartbeat of the business
sections.text: When a member visits a clinician or a provider submits a claim, they rarely think about the technology working behind the scenes to make the experience seamless. But for health plans like Premera, that technology is mission critical.

sections.title: Building for resilience and growth
sections.text: For years, Premera had embraced a cloud-first strategy, but migrating Facets represented an entirely different level of complexity.

sections.title: Raising the stakes
sections.text: The importance of Facets also made the migration inherently risky. Premera simply couldn’t tolerate extended downtime or performance regressions. A failed migration could interrupt claims processing, affecting provider payments and the timely delivery of care for members.

sections.title: A partnership focused on outcomes
sections.text: Microsoft’s partnership helped Premera validate its migration approach and move forward with confidence, supporting a successful transition of a mission-critical platform to Azure with zero data loss and no rollback required.

sections.title: Delivering measurable impact
sections.text: The migration itself represented transformation at true enterprise scale. During production cutover, approximately 54 terabytes of data were migrated while modernizing more than 220 servers, enabling over 2,400 users, and transitioning roughly 1,400 batch processes. Most importantly, the migration was completed with zero data loss and no rollback required.

sections.title: A foundation for the future
sections.text: For Premera, moving Facets to Azure was never the finish line. Instead, it established a stronger operational foundation for continued modernization across the enterprise. The organization is now positioned to build on that success, using its cloud foundation to modernize additional systems and support the next generation of capabilities.

sections.text: Energy companies increasingly seek ways to reduce the administrative burden on frontline workers, who spend valuable time searching documents, interpreting procedures, and completing manual processes.

As leaders look to improve productivity and safety, many are rethinking frontline work. Thousands of documents stand between frontline workers and the hands-on part of their jobs. Whether it’s pulling permits, finding maintenance manuals, or manually filling out forms, hours or days spent in the office could be devoted to inspections and repairs.

sections.text: With most of its workforce in the field, Williams recognized an opportunity to lead with empowerment. The Tulsa, Oklahoma–based natural gas company, which employs 6,000-plus employees, deployed Microsoft 365 Copilot directly to frontline employees. This effort was designed to enhance productivity, simplify daily work, and equip teams with AI as a core capability, helping to simplify processes.

sections.title: Accelerating operations with Copilot
sections.text: Copilot now supports critical operations across Williams. It helps generate plans, interpret procedures, and assess regulatory requirements, reducing manual review and accelerating execution. Copilot not only assists with troubleshooting, decision-making, and safety reporting, but it improves resolution speed, documentation quality, and compliance.

sections.title: Enabling innovation from the field
sections.text: The company is fostering a culture where those closest to the work can shape how technology is applied. As a result, ideas and uses are emerging organically from the field, driving continuous improvement and increasing AI’s impact over time. “We see AI as a critical tool for every Williams employee, and it becomes a force multiplier in how we collaborate, compete, and develop new, innovative, courageous ideas. The partnership with Microsoft is enabling us to transform our workforce to be our superpower,” says Naveen Pandrangi, VP & Chief Transformation and Information Officer, Williams.

sections.title: Driving a broader AI transformation
sections.text: By bringing Copilot directly into frontline operations, Williams is transforming work across its organization, laying the foundation for expanded AI adoption. AI is becoming an accessible tool for employees in the field, helping them work faster, make better decisions, and operate more effectively in complex, high-stakes environments. It may well extend beyond frontline operations into a broader end-to-end AI journey.

title: Avanade cuts incident resolution time by up to 80% with Microsoft Security Copilot

sections.title: Executive summary
sections.text: As AI adoption accelerated across the professional services industry, Avanade needed to modernize identity-driven security operations and scale security expertise beyond what traditional investigation workflows could support.

sections.title: READ THE STORY
sections.text: Professional services firms are moving quickly to help clients adopt AI, and that shift is raising the bar for their own security operations. Clients want advisors that can speak from experience along with strategy. For firms guiding enterprise transformation, secure and scalable AI operations are becoming part of the value proposition. Trust, governance, and operational resilience are core differentiators amidst accelerated AI adoption.

sections.title: Secure AI operations start with identity
sections.text: As a leading global professional services firm, Avanade faced these same pressures firsthand. The pace of AI adoption was increasing faster than traditional identity investigation workflows could support. Avanade needed to modernize its identity-driven security operations and scale security expertise to match the speed of its own enterprise AI adoption.

sections.title: Bringing AI into daily identity investigations
sections.text: Avanade addressed this challenge by embedding Microsoft Security Copilot into daily identity and access management operations with Microsoft Entra. Engineers used Security Copilot during live identity investigations to bring together identity signals, investigator guidance, and recommended next steps in a single workflow. Rather than gathering context manually across multiple tools and screens, analysts could focus on decisions and resolution. This brought AI into the workflow where identity investigations already happened.

sections.title: Turning expertise into a repeatable workflow
sections.text: “Microsoft Security Copilot helped us bring the right identity signals together during active triage, so engineers could consistently move from investigation to resolution much faster. The speed is important, but the consistency matters just as much.”

sections.title: Expanding AI-assisted security operations
sections.text: Security Copilot became part of the identity operations team’s daily workflow at scale as Avanade continued building the secure operational foundation needed to support AI adoption. The impact became especially visible during Avanade’s passkey rollout to approximately 17,000 users. Identity teams used Security Copilot to help focus on passkey-related issues, provide faster resolutions, and manage more than 180 passkey adoption–related support tickets per day. As those AI-assisted workflows became part of daily identity operations, Avanade applied a similar approach to security operations.

sections.title: Custom agents transform security operations
sections.text: To expand AI-assisted workflows across security operations, Avanade built custom agents on top of the Security Copilot platform to support its unique investigations and workflows. The agents consolidate security signals, recommendations, and playbook-based next steps for analysts. In doing so, they capture documented institutional knowledge and codify workflows, helping scale security expertise throughout the investigation process.

sections.title: Expanding an agentic security foundation
sections.text: “Microsoft Security Copilot has helped our identity operations team work smarter and move faster. By turning expert knowledge into repeatable, AI-assisted workflows, we reduced resolution times by up to 80% and enabled the team to take on more work with greater consistency and confidence.”

sections.title: Executive summary
sections.text: Pamarco's lean finance organization saw its month-end close process becoming more complex and time-consuming in recent years, leaving finance professionals with less time for analysis and strategic decision-making.

sections.title: Global manufacturing depends on lean operations
sections.text: Pamarco supplies precision-engineered anilox rolls, blades, accessories, and technical services to printing and packaging businesses. Its products support corrugated packaging, flexible packaging, coating and laminating, and towel and tissue production. With approximately 225 employees, operations in the United States and Europe, and customers in almost 70 countries, the company combines a global reach with a deliberately lean operating model.

sections.title: A longer close limits business insight
sections.text: Pamarco's finance organization is small and decentralized. Accountants and operational leaders often carry responsibilities beyond traditional finance work, so urgent requests can pull attention away from the monthly close. Burgess explains that as the business grows, so does the complexity of the monthly financial close.

sections.title: Bounded agents take on repeatable finance work
sections.text: Pamarco is building autonomous finance workflows with Microsoft Copilot Studio, the Dynamics 365 ERP MCP Server, and Microsoft Dataverse skills. Rather than giving every user unrestricted access to a general-purpose assistant, the company defines agents and skills for specific jobs. Each scenario needs a clearly defined workload, appropriate permissions, and measurable time savings.

sections.title: Cowork turns recurring work into actionable insights
sections.text: Pamarco also uses Copilot Cowork for tightly controlled scheduled work. Wilson created a virtual user that runs daily, weekly, and monthly routines, drawing on sales and manufacturing data from Dynamics 365 to generate recurring reports. Results flow into Microsoft Power BI, Microsoft Excel, Microsoft Word, email, and presentation outputs.

sections.title: More time for proactive financial decisions
sections.text: Finance professionals are shifting from coordinating repetitive tasks to reviewing exceptions and acting on information. Scheduled reports arrive without the same manual assembly effort, invoice coding handles routine cases, and autonomous close tasks advance when their dependencies are ready.

sections.title: Knowledge continuity and adoption
sections.text: An added benefit is the reduced risk of losing operational knowledge as experienced employees retire or move into different roles. By placing repeatable knowledge into governed agents connected to Dynamics 365, the company can make critical routines less dependent on any one person while keeping experts accountable for the final decision.

sections.title: Extending agents into commercial operations
sections.text: Pamarco plans to deepen finance automation and then extend the pattern into sales, quoting, order entry, customer response, and vendor communications. The company sees particular value in using historical transactions and pricing information to improve quotations, reduce unexpected outcomes, and respond to customers more consistently. Planned customer-facing scenarios will follow the same requirement for defined access, controlled actions, and measurable value.

sections.title: READ THE STORY
sections.text: Enterprises execute billions of agreements every year. Buried inside are renewal deadlines, pricing terms, obligations, and risk indicators that shape business decisions, but surfacing that intelligence has historically required manual review.

sections.title: A foundation for innovation at scale
sections.text: To help customers unlock intelligence hidden within their agreements, Docusign first built its Intelligent Agreement Management (IAM) on Microsoft Azure, scaling agreement intelligence across millions of documents on a platform designed for innovation, efficiency, and growth.

Larger foundation models act as “teacher” models, generating high-quality training data across a wide range of agreement types. That data is validated and used to fine-tune smaller models, which are evaluated before deployment and continuously monitored in production.

sections.title: Scaling AI with enterprise trust
sections.text: Agreement data is among the most sensitive information that organizations handle, often subject to regulatory and residency requirements. Docusign processes data in-region using Azure services and isolates workloads at the tenant level on AKS, helping ensure customer data remains highly secure and separated.

sections.title: From agreement intelligence to business action
sections.text: Today, IAM processes over 1 million agreement documents each day, transforming agreement content into structured data that organizations can use to make decisions, automate workflows, and drive business outcomes. For users, the impact is immediate.

title: To innovate faster, BNY upskills 100% of staff on Eliza, powered by Microsoft AI
description: Through a tiered upskilling program, BNY taught nearly 50,000 employees AI-literacy and reached 100% adoption of its AI platform, Eliza.

sections.title: Executive summary
sections.text: BNY is a 242-year-old bank that oversees approximately $60 trillion on behalf of clients across 100 markets. The next step in this storied firm’s history? Training its massive global workforce of nearly 50,000 employees on modern AI tools.

sections.title: READ THE STORY
sections.text: When it comes to training nearly 50,000 employees, the bank took a democratic approach. “We knew that AI was not only going to be a technological revolution, it was going to be a cultural revolution for BNY,” says Russell.

sections.title: A platform approach to AI in partnership with Microsoft
sections.text: Eliza is BNY’s in-house AI platform, “named after the well-known philanthropist and wife of our founder, Alexander Hamilton,” Romanoff shares. “When we started our generative AI journey, we made a deliberate decision to create a platform approach,” he says. This was a key decision in developing the tool, as Eliza now serves as a governance platform, provides AI tools and agent building capabilities and, crucially for the early days of AI literacy, is also a learning platform.

sections.title: 400,000 hours of training delivered for an AI-literate workforce
sections.text: After completing training on AI fundamentals—the Explorer tier—the Builder tier introduces more complex uses. Finally, the Pioneer level is a select group of change agents who complete a 40-hour bootcamp focused on agentic AI. “This is where people learn to rewire their workflows with AI,” says Shonnar. The bootcamps have scaled from 200 to 800 participants per cohort, a mark of the program’s success. “The idea is to prepare these AI Pioneers to help people within their teams,” says Shonnar.

sections.title: Communication and engagement for enterprise-wide adoption
sections.text: The communication angle in BNY’s change management strategy includes top-down and bottoms-up support. “We have AI leadership at the very top as well as a lot of enthusiasm and insights from all levels of the business,” says Romanoff. “Everyone on our executive committee has been hands-on with AI,” adds Russell. “That has been really important for our journey.”

sections.title: Addressing AI skepticism through hands-on learning
sections.text: Shonnar notes that BNY approached AI literacy with an emphasis on humans. “This is about augmenting human capability, allowing us to do a lot more, focus on strategic decision making, engaging clients, and doing less of the mundane, repetitive tasks,” he says. With that in mind, trainings prioritize business outcomes. And, to keep the courses as relevant as possible, BNY has implemented a quarterly curriculum review.

sections.title: 100% of employees trained on in-house AI platform
sections.text: Today, Eliza is the go-to platform at BNY. “We now have 100% of our employees trained to use Eliza and almost two-thirds of employees who are daily or ‘super’ users of AI at the bank,” says Russell. “Additionally, almost 60% of the organization has been onboarded to Microsoft 365 Copilot.”

sections.title: Executive summary
sections.text: Atlanta Public Schools tracked referrals, transcripts, transportation requests, and procurement on spreadsheets, paper forms, and email chains, straining staff time and limiting visibility across departments.

sections.title: READ THE STORY
sections.text: At Atlanta Public Schools (APS), timely, accurate information helps school psychologists, administrators, and support teams better serve students. sections.title: Choosing to build, not buy

sections.title: Returning time to students
sections.text: Today, the referral application provides a single view of caseloads, timelines, and student information. Built-in validation checks, automated reminders, and digitized records reduce manual work while helping staff maintain accurate information and timely evaluations.

sections.title: Extending the model across student services

sections.title: About Canlak Coatings
sections.text: Canlak Coatings is a North American manufacturer of wood coatings, serving customers across multiple markets from its base in New Jersey. It is a mid-sized business, and it had already done the unglamorous work that most companies put off: for close to two years it had run its daily reporting on Microsoft Fabric, on a governed Power BI semantic model used across the company, with an enterprise data warehouse, a governed gold layer on the medallion architecture, running on Microsoft OneLake.

sections.title: The Challenge: Plan_use_this_final.xlsx
sections.text: Sales forecasting sat outside that foundation entirely. The forecast lived in a spreadsheet and worked at the sales rep and customer level, but moving it to the product level created more tabs, links, and manual reconciliation against daily product-level actuals in Fabric. The forecast was refreshed infrequently, while actuals moved daily.

sections.title: Extend the platform, do not add another one
sections.text: Canlak Coatings sought to extend the governed platform already used for reporting into planning instead of introducing a separate forecasting system. Its goal was a rolling, product-level forecast using the same data, definitions, and security as daily reporting.

sections.title: Inside the solution
sections.text: With Data Crafters, Canlak Coatings placed Planning in Microsoft Fabric on top of its existing enterprise data warehouse in OneLake. Data flows through Microsoft Fabric pipelines into OneLake and the governed Power BI semantic model, which feeds both Power BI reports and the Fabric Planning sheet.

sections.title: What changed for Canlak Coatings
sections.text: The forecast cycle decreased from three to four weeks to approximately one week, described as a 75 to 80 percent reduction in the time finance spends producing each cycle. Forecast granularity moved from customer level to product level with no manual reconciliation because plan and actuals use one semantic model. Canlak Coatings gained a rolling 12-month view refreshed monthly, with no increase in platform cost or noticeable increase in capacity consumption.

sections.title: The road ahead
sections.text: Canlak Coating's established data foundation, single semantic model, inherited security, and single source of truth enabled it to add enterprise sales planning in under four weeks. Finance users now enter forecast figures in the Fabric Planning sheet on a monthly cycle that preserves full-year visibility.
